title: Networking in Compose
idea: By default, Compose puts every service on one private network. Services reach each other by service name, such as `db`, not by IP address.
points: `up` creates the network `<project>_default`. The project name defaults to your folder's name.
Docker's built-in DNS turns a service name into the container's IP address.
Services talk on the container port; `ports` only matters for traffic from outside.
Custom `networks` split services: two services can talk only if they share a network.

hero.title: Services find each other by name

steps.caption: In a folder named `bookstore`, `up` creates the network `bookstore_default` and joins both services.
`api` connects to host `db`, port 5432. Docker's DNS turns `db` into the container's IP address.
Publishing port 3000 on `api` lets your machine reach it at `localhost:3000`.
`db` publishes nothing, so `localhost:5432` on your machine does not reach it. Only services on the network can.
Publish `db` as `5433:5432` and your machine uses 5433. `api` still connects to `db:5432`.

code.title: Default network
code.caption: No `networks` key, so both services join the default network. Put `DB_PASSWORD` in a `.env` file.

walk.text: Publish `api` to your machine. `db` has no `ports`, so only services can reach it.
The host in the URL is `db`, the service name. `localhost` would mean `api` itself.
`5432` is the container port Postgres listens on. Services use it, whatever the host port.

code.title: Custom networks
code.caption: A fragment: only the network keys. Each service lists the networks it joins.

walk.text: `api` joins both networks, so it reaches `proxy` and `db`.
Top-level `networks` declares them. Compose names them `<project>_front` and `<project>_back`.

pitfalls: `db` resolves only inside the network; from your laptop use `localhost` and a published port.
Publish `db` only when you must, as `127.0.0.1:5432:5432`, so other machines cannot connect.
Use service names, never container IPs: Docker assigns addresses dynamically.

quiz.q: Service `db` is published as `5433:5432`. What host and port should `api` use for it?
quiz.why: Services use the service name and the container port. Host port 5433 is for your machine, and `localhost` inside `api` means `api`.

takeaway: Inside Compose, call services by name and use the container port.
